summary: Module 4 VERIFY: Edge Case Testing with committed regression tests. Ran the module's 5 edge case tests against the team endpoints live: (1) add already-member -> 409 'user is already a member' (both pre-check and IntegrityError path); (2) create team with empty/whitespace name -> 400 request_invalid; (3) add member without auth -> 401 unauthorized; (4) non-member/owner-only actions (add, list, patch role) as Bob -> 403 forbidden on all three; (5) invalid email 'not-an-email' -> 400 request_invalid. ALL 5 EXPECTED RESULTS OBSERVED. The module's warning applies: all tests passed, so I had to prove they are NOT vacuous -- since the team feature had ZERO committed tests (only live probes), I wrote tests/test_teams.py with 17 real assertions: auth required (401), owner_id present (201), empty/space/overlong names (400), owner-or-admin enforcement (403), duplicate add (409), owner self-add (409), unknown user (404), invalid email (400), invalid role (400), list owner-only (403/200), list shows added users with role, admin CAN add but CANNOT change roles (403 owner-only), role change owner-only (403/200), remove owner-only (403/204), nonexistent team (404), case-sensitive role literal (400). Full suite now 92 tests, exit 0 (was 75). The verification is now non-vacuous: these tests would fail if any security check were stubbed out (e.g., remove the require_owner call and test_remove_member_owner_only fails).
evidence: Full suite: 92 tests, exit 0 (75 before + 17 new)
Non-vacuous proof: each test asserts an exact status + semantics, not just 'not 500'
